newsitem.title: GREECE: Cyprus bourse on course for computerisation.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus bourse on course for computerisation.

text.p: The Cyprus Stock Exchange, which started operations in March last year, is working to introduce fully computerised trading and hopes to usher in paperless settlement early in 1998, its president, Dinos Papadopoulos said in a speech to Greece's financial community on Friday.

"We have acquired a system by Australian company Computershare Systems Pty Ltd. The contract was signed recently and completion of the project is expected in the first semester of 1998," Papadopoulos said.
"It is an ambitious project which among other things will result in the establishment of a central register for all listed shares registered in Cyprus."
Capitalised at 1.1 billion Cyprus pounds ($556.9 million), or 26 percent of 1996 GDP, the Cyprus exchange deals in 88 securities from 43 listed companies.
Average daily trading volume last year reached 670,000 Cyprus pounds, rising further in the first months of 1997 to 810,000 Cyprus pounds.
Before the official launch of the exchange, the Cyprus equities market was an over-the-counter market. Since the launch, settlement has been shortened significantly to trade-date-plus-nine (T+9).
Papadopoulos told Greek brokers and institutional investors that a bill on insider trading is awaiting a vote by parliament soon and will complete the regulatory framework for the exchange.

The island of Cyprus has been divided since 1974 between a Turkish Cypriot northern sector and a Greek Cypriot-led government in Nicosia which is moving towards talks on entry into the European Union.
Papadopoulos said that despite its political difficulties the island's economy has managed high growth rates and macroeconomic indicators which satisfy the EU's Maastricht treaty targets.
He said that Cyprus's strategic location between Europe, the Middle East and Africa, made it "a bridge in the wider region's business environment."
He said it had developed into an off-shore centre and aims to list some off-shore companies, including off-shore funds, on the exchange.
Cyprus' central bank is looking into a bill that will outline the operating framework of foreign mutual funds and their listing on the exchange.
Recently, constraints on Greek and other foreign investment in Cyprus listings have been eased as maximum stakes have been raised.

Procedures have also been simplified and no longer require central bank approval prior to any trade on the Cyprus stock exchange by foreign investors. And Cyprus banks have begun to offer custodial services to facilitate foreign investment activities, Papadopoulos said.
"It should be noted that there is express interest for the listing of Greek companies -- already listed on the Athens bourse -- on the Cyprus stock exchange and vice-versa," he said.
"We should intensify our efforts on this front to implement cross-listings." --Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 ($ = 1.975 Cyprus Pounds)
